title: Yaku Pérez vigil outside the CNE amid a demand for vote recount
location: Outside the National Electoral Council (CNE) command center, Quito
organizer: Yaku Pérez; the report does not identify a separate organizing group
threshold_50_evidence: Unknown; the article reports a vigil but no attendee count.

start_date.summary: The Ecuavisa body reports Pérez kept a vigil outside the CNE on 8 February 2021.

location.summary: Outside the CNE command center in Quito.

organizer.summary: Pérez is reported keeping the vigil; a separate organizer is not identified.

demands.summary: The vigil called for ballot boxes in Manabí, Pichincha and Guayas to be opened and votes recounted individually.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: Unknown; no group size is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The article does not establish whether violence occurred.

state_response.summary: The CNE president says a recount is possible if requirements are met, but the report does not describe a response to or accommodation of the gathering; all response variables remain unknown.

notes: This is a verified physical vigil with an explicit process demand, but it is not yet eligible because the public-attendance threshold is unknown. The CNE president’s procedural statement is not coded as a concession.
open_questions: Can a public turnout of at least 50 be verified?
What was the physical end of the vigil?
Is this separate from or continuous with the 10 February CNE demonstrations?

title: Pachakutik supporters demonstrate at CNE offices in Quito and Guayaquil over an election recount
location: CNE locations in Quito and Guayaquil; in Quito, two electoral centers and a march to CNE headquarters
organizer: Pachakutik militants/supporters; formal event organizer not separately identified
participants_original: Expreso reports hundreds overall at the CNE offices; Guayaquil was the larger concentration. In Quito, about 200 people marched from two electoral centers to CNE headquarters.
threshold_50_evidence: About 200 people in the Quito march alone, a reported approximate count exceeding 50.

start_date.summary: Expreso dates the peaceful demonstrations in Quito and Guayaquil to Wednesday, 10 February 2021.

location.summary: CNE offices in Quito and Guayaquil; Quito participants gathered at two electoral centers and marched to CNE headquarters.

organizer.summary: The article identifies Pachakutik militants and supporters; it does not name a formal organizer for each city gathering.

demands.summary: Participants protested an alleged electoral fraud and Pérez said he would seek a vote-by-vote recount.

participants_original.summary: The article reports hundreds overall; the larger concentration was in Guayaquil. It gives an approximate 200 people for the Quito march.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: About 200 people marched in Quito to CNE headquarters, an explicit approximate count above 50.

end_date.summary: No physical closing time or dispersal is reported.

protester_violence.summary: The article explicitly describes the demonstrations as peaceful.

state_response.summary: No state response to these gatherings is reported; silence is not coded as ignore.

notes: A physical, demand-driven assembly is directly described: the article identifies an allegation of electoral fraud and a recount request at CNE offices, not only electoral support. Keep the candidate/supporter context visible for coordinator review. Do not merge automatically with the 8 February vigil or the later reported Loja–Quito march.
open_questions: Should the Quito and Guayaquil actions be treated as one coordinated multi-city event or distinct local actions?
Does the documented recount demand distinguish this event from an exclusively candidate-support rally under the original codebook?
What were the physical end and state response?
Is there continuity with the 8 February vigil or later march?
